issues.display_title: Issue #392: Bug: object list groups by type instead of newest→oldest (PRD #291)
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor object list ordering bug. Unmet AC of #291 ("Objects are sorted newest to oldest").

Description

The All object list should be ordered newest→oldest across all types. Instead it's grouped by type (Points, then Polygons, then Circles, then Rectangles…) — see screenshot.

Root cause

src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts: buildEditorObjects (L142–173) assigns each object's order from a single running counter walked over a fixed per-type traversal (walls → areas → doors → windows → rect → circle → polygon → points → safety → panoramas). So order encodes type-grouping, not real creation order; sortNewestFirst (L87, b.order - a.order) just reverses the type blocks — still grouped.

Object ids are crypto.randomUUID() (interactions.ts), so no creation order is recoverable from existing data. The code comment (L138–140) already flags this: "no per-object creation timestamp in the model … A real backend created-at would make global newest-first exact."

Approach (FE-only, no BE change)

  • Add an optional monotonic createdAt (Date.now()-based) to objects at each create site, thread it into buildEditorObjects, and sort by it (desc) so cross-type newest-first is exact for newly created objects.
  • Legacy objects (no createdAt) fall back to the current type-traversal order — documented limitation; a BE created_at would make it exact for old projects too.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Newly created objects list strictly newest→oldest across all types (not type-grouped).
  • Per-type filters + counts + search unchanged.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

NOTE — decided approach: Option C (BE-authoritative created_at)

Chosen over the FE-only Option A. Server assigns created_at, so ordering is consistent across clients and stored structurally. Plan for Monday:

Backend — Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO

  • On project save (the canvas_data / floorplan blob), parse the objects per type — walls, areas/rooms, doors, windows, shapes (rect/circle/polygon), points, safety annotations, panoramas — and assign a monotonic created_at (server clock or a per-project sequence) to any object lacking one, keyed by object id. Write it back into the blob.
  • Coupling caveat: the BE parser now depends on the FE object schema. Whenever FE adds an object type/field, the parser must follow. Keep a single shared shape doc.
  • Migration: backfill created_at for all existing projects' blobs. Order for legacy objects is best-effort / type-grouped — there is no historical creation timestamp, so old projects can't be made exact (same limitation as any option).

Frontend — src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts

  • Sort by created_at desc in sortNewestFirst / buildEditorObjects instead of the type-traversal order; fall back to the current order when created_at is absent.
  • Hybrid recommended: FE also stamps a provisional created_at at object-create time (see create sites: editor/interactions.ts L42/60/87/88, editor/interaction-tools.ts L167/30/104, editor/commands.ts L71/94), and BE only fills gaps / normalizes. Reason ↓.

Socket — gothru-maps-socket

  • No change. edit.handler.ts relays an opaque snapshot string (2 MB cap) + version counter; it never parses objects, so created_at rides inside the blob automatically.
  • Edge case to handle: objects created during a live collab session sync via socket without hitting BE save, so they won't get a server created_at until the next BE persist → ordering is provisional until save. The FE-provisional stamp (hybrid above) fixes this: the object has a stable local created_at immediately, BE just canonicalizes on save.

Reality check (applies to A and C alike)

  • Existing objects have no historical creation timestamp anywhere — legacy projects can only be backfilled with best-effort/arbitrary order. Only objects created after the fix get true newest-first.

Discussion: A and C give identical real-world results (legacy can't be fixed; new objects correct). C is chosen for server-authoritative consistency, at the cost of a BE parser + migration + FE↔BE schema coupling.

RESULT

Shipped as Option C (FE stamps, backend canonicalizes). PR #401 (commits 4c6f8ae, 044af88), merged to development.

  • Optional createdAt (epoch ms) added to every object type on both the store models (useMapStore.types.ts) and the engine models (floorplan/types.ts), carried through the levelToModel / modelToLevel round trip (bridge.ts).
  • Stamped in modelToLevel — the single choke point every editor change passes through before persistence and before the collab snapshot — so it covers walls, doors and windows too, which have no id of their own, without touching each create site.
  • Only objects new to this model are stamped. First cut stamped everything unstamped, which handed the object just created the same timestamp as all the legacy ones; the tie then fell back to per-type order — the exact grouping being fixed (and worst for walls/doors/windows/shapes, whose traversal position is early). "New" = absent from prev: positionally for walls/doors/windows, by id for areas/points/safety/shapes. Legacy objects stay unstamped, which sorts as oldest.
  • sortNewestFirst keys on createdAt, with the per-type order demoted to tiebreak.

Known limitation (unavoidable): objects created before this ships have no creation time recorded anywhere — FE, BE or socket — so they keep their type-grouped relative order. Everything created from now on sorts correctly newest-first across types.

Backend counterpart: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#117 (PR #118, merged). Socket: no change — it relays an opaque snapshot, so createdAt rides inside it.

19 objectRows + 12 bridge tests; tsc / eslint green.

issues.display_title: Issue #403: Editor: canvas should auto-grow to fit objects outside the floorplan image bounds
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor canvas sizing.

Description

The plan canvas (the framed "page" the floorplan sits on) is exactly the size of the floorplan image. Any object drawn past that frame — a wall dragged to the right, a shape placed below — sits outside the page: it falls outside the frame, outside the grid, and Fit ignores it when computing zoom, so it can end up off-screen.

The canvas should auto-grow to cover every object, while the floorplan image stays exactly where it is (same position, same size — it must not stretch or shift).

Root cause

model.w / model.h are the page size, and they are adopted verbatim from the backdrop image's pixel dimensions — adoptBackdropSize() → scaleModelToSize(model, bgImage.naturalWidth, bgImage.naturalHeight) (model-sync.ts:176).

Everything that renders the page reads that rect directly:

  • backdrop image — draw.ts:43
  • grid lines 0 … model.w / 0 … model.h — draw.ts:48-49
  • page frame strokeRect(ox, oy, model.w * sc, model.h * sc) — draw.ts:51
  • fit-to-view zoom + centering — view.ts:22-23

So page == image, and there is no notion of content extending beyond it.

model.w/model.h must not be grown to fix this: S = max(model.w, model.h) is the model's normalization scale for real-world wall widths and opening spans (model-sync.ts:122, interaction-tools.ts:24), for the 3D scene framing (scene3d.ts:106) and for the level bridge (bridge.ts:174). Changing it would silently resize every wall and door in the model, and stretch the backdrop image.

Scope

  • Add a pure helper that returns the canvas bounds — the union of the image rect (0, 0, model.w, model.h) and the bounding box of all content: walls (incl. bezier handles), doors, windows, icons, manual areas, points, safety marks, shapes, room labels. Grows on all four sides, so objects at negative coordinates are covered too.
  • Use those bounds for the page frame, the grid extent, and fit-to-view (zoom + centering).
  • Leave the backdrop image drawn at world (0,0)–(model.w, model.h) — unchanged position and size.
  • Derived at render time only: nothing new persisted, no model mutation, no migration, no backend/socket change. Old projects get the behaviour for free.
  • Add a small padding margin so objects sitting exactly on the new edge aren't flush against the frame.

Acceptance Criteria

  • An object dragged past the image edge (any direction) grows the frame + grid to include it; the object is never outside the page.
  • The floorplan image does not move, resize, or stretch when the canvas grows.
  • Fit frames all content, including objects outside the image rect.
  • With all content inside the image rect, the canvas is exactly the image rect — unchanged from today.
  • Wall widths, door/window spans and the 3D scene are unaffected (model.w/model.h untouched).
  • Unit test for the bounds helper (image-only, content outside, negative coordinates).
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

The plan page is now derived rather than being the backdrop image rect.

New pure helper canvasBounds(model, pad) in src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts returns the union of the image rect (0, 0, model.w, model.h) and the bounding box of all content — walls (including bezier control handles), doors, windows, icons, manual areas, points, safety marks and shapes. It grows on all four sides, so objects at negative coordinates are covered too. pad is applied only to the content extremes, so a floor whose objects all sit inside the image rect returns exactly that rect — identical to the previous behaviour.

view.ts exposes planBounds(model) = canvasBounds(model, GRID) as the single source, used by:

  • fit2D — zoom + centering now frame the page (ox/oy still resolve to the screen position of world (0,0), just offset by -b.x * sc).
  • draw.ts — the page frame strokeRect and the grid extent. Grid lines stay anchored to world 0 (Math.ceil(b.x / GRID) * GRID) so they don't shift as the page grows.

The backdrop image still draws at ctx.ox, ctx.oy with size model.w × model.h — unchanged position and size. Every other consumer of ox/oy (w2s, s2w, zoomAt, pan) already treated them as the world origin, so none needed touching.

model.w/model.h were deliberately left alone: they are the model's normalization scale S = max(w, h) for wall widths, opening spans, the 3D scene and the level bridge — growing them would have silently rescaled the whole floor and stretched the backdrop.

Derived at render time only. Nothing new is persisted, no model mutation, no migration, and no backend or socket change — existing projects get the behaviour for free.

Files

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts — canvasBounds()

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/index.ts — re-export

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/view.ts — planBounds(), fit2D

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts — frame + grid

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/canvas-bounds.test.ts — 7 new tests (image-only, all content inside, growth right/bottom, negative coordinates, curved walls, every object kind, non-finite coordinates)

  • Branch: feature/403-canvas-auto-grow · Commit: 37cae46

  • pnpm test (7 new green), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green. The 2 suite failures (renameSweep.test.ts, api/upload/route.test.ts EACCES on /tmp) pre-date this branch and are unrelated.

issues.display_title: Issue #405: Bug: doors and windows don't follow their wall when it is moved or dragged
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor wall/opening bug.

Description

Moving a wall leaves its doors and windows behind.

  • Drag the wall body — the wall translates, the door/window stays floating at its old position, no longer on any wall.
  • Drag a wall endpoint (stretch / rotate) — same: the wall line changes, the opening keeps its old absolute coordinates and ends up off the wall, sometimes past its new end.

A door or window belongs to the wall it was cut into. It must stay on that wall, at the same relative position along it, whenever the wall moves.

Root cause

On pointer-down over a wall, the drag set ctx.pending is built only from the selected walls' own endpoints plus their curve handles (interactions.ts:188-192):

ctx.pending = dedupeRefs(ctx.selWalls.flatMap((w) => [
  ...joinGroup(ctx, { o: w, kx: "x1", ky: "y1" }),
  ...joinGroup(ctx, { o: w, kx: "x2", ky: "y2" }),
  ...(w.h1x !== undefined ? [{ o: w, kx: "h1x", ky: "h1y" }, { o: w, kx: "h2x", ky: "h2y" }] as PointRef[] : []),
]));

joinGroup is pointsAt(model, x, y, JOIN_EPS) (hittest.ts:11) — it collects every endpoint coincident with the wall's own endpoint, within JOIN_EPS = 3. Door/window endpoints are in that candidate set (editing.ts:11-22), but an opening cut into the middle of a wall is nowhere near either wall endpoint, so it is never picked up. The move loop then translates only what is in ctx.drag (interactions.ts:257) — the wall moves, the opening does not.

The endpoint-drag path (interactions.ts:163) has the same gap, and is worse: it changes the wall's length and angle, so even translating the opening by the same delta would be wrong — it has to be re-placed along the new wall line.

The wall↔opening association already exists and is not the missing piece: wallForOpening(model, op, tolPx) (editing.ts:32) resolves the wall an opening lies on (collinear + overlapping) and is already used by the align commands (commands.ts:103). The drag path just never consults it.

Scope

  • At pointer-down on a wall (body drag and endpoint drag), resolve the openings attached to each affected wall via wallForOpening, and record for each one its parametric position on that wall — the centre t along the wall plus its own length — captured against the wall's pre-drag geometry.
  • After each drag frame moves the wall endpoints, re-place every attached opening at its recorded centre t on the wall's new line, keeping its length and taking the wall's new orientation. alignOpeningOnWall (editing.ts:42) already does this for the left/centre/right presets — the same maths, at an arbitrary t.
  • Keep the opening's length fixed (a door has a real physical width — shrinking a wall must not shrink its door) and clamp it to stay inside the wall.
  • Applies to a multi-wall selection and to walls selected by marquee, not just a single click.
  • Endpoints shared between two walls (joinGroup) already drag both walls together; openings on either wall must follow.
  • Straight walls only — openings can't be placed on curved walls today (interactions.ts:108 skips h1x !== undefined).
  • Undo/redo must restore wall and openings together (the drag already opens one pushUndo per gesture, so one entry covers both).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Dragging a wall body moves its doors and windows with it; each keeps its position along the wall and its size.
  • Dragging a wall endpoint (stretch or rotate) keeps each opening at the same relative position along the wall, re-oriented onto the new wall line, at its original length.
  • Shortening a wall does not shrink its openings; an opening that would fall off the end is clamped to stay on the wall.
  • Openings on a wall dragged as part of a multi-wall / marquee selection follow too.
  • Openings on both walls of a shared, dragged corner follow.
  • A single undo restores the wall and its openings to their pre-drag state.
  • Unrelated openings (on other walls) are untouched.
  • Unit test for the parametric re-placement (translate, stretch, rotate, clamp at the wall end).
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Openings are now anchored to their wall for the whole drag gesture, instead of being left behind.

Pure helpers — src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/editing.ts:

  • openingParamOnWall(op, wall) → { t, len, forward }: the opening's centre position along the wall, its own length, and whether it is stored pointing the same way as the wall.
  • placeOpeningOnWall(op, wall, at): puts it back at that spot on the wall's current geometry. Length is kept and only capped at the wall's own length; the centre is clamped so the opening can never hang off either end; forward is restored so door swing rendering doesn't flip.

Wiring — src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interactions.ts:

  • captureOpeningsOnDraggedWalls(ctx, drag) runs once, when the drag commits, and records an anchor per opening against the wall's pre-drag geometry. It resolves the wall via the existing wallForOpening() — the association was already there, the drag path just never consulted it.
  • Each drag frame re-places every anchored opening from its captured anchor, not by the frame delta. That is what makes an endpoint drag work: a stretch or rotate changes the wall's length and angle, where a delta would be wrong by construction.
  • ctx.openingDrag on EditorContext, cleared in endPointer alongside the other drag state.

Both drag paths are covered because the capture keys off the walls present in ctx.drag: the wall-body path, the endpoint path, multi-wall and marquee selections, and shared corners (joinGroup already puts both walls in the set, so openings on either follow).

Openings already being dragged directly (their own endpoints are in the drag set) are skipped — otherwise dragging a door whose endpoint sits on a wall corner would be pinned by the re-place. Curved walls are skipped too: openings can't be placed on them, and wallForOpening only understands the straight chord.

Undo needed no change — the gesture already opens a single pushUndo, and the history snapshot includes doors/windows, so one undo restores the wall and its openings together.

Files

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/editing.ts — openingParamOnWall(), placeOpeningOnWall(), OpeningOnWall

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/index.ts — re-exports

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/context.ts — openingDrag

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/index.ts — init

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interactions.ts — capture + re-place

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/opening-on-wall.test.ts — 10 new tests (capture, direction, round-trip, translate, stretch, rotate, direction preserved, clamp at the end, wall shorter than the door, degenerate wall)

  • Branch: feature/405-openings-follow-wall · Commit: 3370968

  • pnpm test (10 new green), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green. The 2 suite failures (renameSweep.test.ts, api/upload/route.test.ts EACCES on /tmp) pre-date this branch and are unrelated.

issues.display_title: Issue #407: Editor: restyle door / window / shape colours, and thicken walls and doors
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor 2D canvas restyle.

Description

Restyle the 2D plan canvas so doors, windows and shapes use the new palette, and so walls and doors read as heavier elements.

Object Outline Fill
Door #EE118A #EEC7E7
Window #2C9599 — (keeps its current glass render)
Shape (rectangle, circle, polygon) #FA9E3D #EFD3C8

Walls and doors are drawn thicker. The wall stays a line — a heavier stroke, not a filled band.

Current state

All three colours are hardcoded in palette.ts:

C.door = "rgba(5, 150, 105, 1)";   C.win = "rgba(2, 132, 199, 1)";      // L33 — emerald / sky
C.shapeFill = "rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.10)"; C.shapeStroke = "rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.75)";   // L43 — indigo

The Palette type lives in context.ts:10-17. There is no doorFill token — the door is currently drawn as a dashed stroked line only (draw.ts:83-91), so there is nothing to fill yet.

Current stroke widths (draw.ts):

  • wall — 3 / hover 4 / selected 5 (L151)
  • door — 3.5 / hover 4.5 / selected 5, dashed (L89)
  • window — two parallel lines 1.6 apart, width 2 / selected 2.6 (L133-135)
  • shape — 1.25 / selected 2 (L254)

Scope

  • Repoint C.door, C.win, C.shapeFill, C.shapeStroke in palette.ts to the colours above, and add a C.doorFill token (plus its Palette field in context.ts).
  • Door becomes a filled band along its span — #EEC7E7 fill, #EE118A outline — instead of a dashed line, and thicker than today. Its swing arc + leaf keep the outline colour.
  • Wall stroke gets thicker but stays a stroked line (straight and bezier alike). No fill, no band.
  • Window keeps its two-parallel-line glass render, recoloured to #2C9599 and thickened to sit alongside the new wall/door weights.
  • Shape fill/outline follow the new tokens for every kind (rect, circle, polygon), including the in-progress draft (draw.ts:283), the multi-select bounding box (draw.ts:267-273) and the resize handles (draw-helpers.ts:36).
  • Endpoint handles that stroke in C.door / C.win (draw.ts:123, draw.ts:142) and the add-tool preview (draw.ts:410) pick the new colours up for free — verify, don't duplicate.
  • Hover and selected states stay --foreground / --primary (C.hot / C.sel) so selection is still obvious against the new colours.
  • Hit-test tolerances are independent of stroke width, so thicker strokes must not change what is clickable.

Notes / decisions

  • Only the DEFAULT shape colour changes — a shape stays recolourable. Every consumer reads shape.color ?? <default> (draw.ts:253, scene3d.ts:243, geojson-utils.ts:497, selection.ts:42), so the per-shape colour picker keeps working exactly as it does now. Shapes the user already recoloured keep their colour; only the unset default moves.
  • The four colours are fixed hex, not theme tokens — same as the door/window colours they replace. #EEC7E7 and #EFD3C8 are pale, so check they still read on the dark-mode canvas (the backdrop is inverted in dark mode, draw.ts:42).
  • The 3D scene and the map follow the new shape colour too (confirmed in scope). Only shapes are affected there: doors and windows carry no colour in 3D or on the map — they are cut-outs in the wall geometry (wallOpenings() → holes; a window is a wall gap with a sill + header), so there is nothing to recolour. See the "3D + map" section below.
  • Thickness stays editor-canvas only. The map and the 3D scene render walls as real volumes sized by WALL_W, not as strokes, so there is no stroke weight there to thicken.
  • Exact new stroke widths are a visual call; land a first pass and tune against the design.

3D + map (shape colour follow-through)

SHAPE_COLOR = "#8a7a5c" (constants.ts:13) is the single default behind all three non-canvas surfaces. Repointing it to the new shape fill covers:

  • the 3D scene mesh — scene3d.ts:243
  • the map's flat fill + extrusion — geojson-utils.ts:497 feeds ["get", "color"] in layer-definitions.ts
  • the colour swatch the shape panel shows as the default — selection.ts:42

Watch out: SHAPE_COLOR is currently a dark muted brown, chosen so furniture reads against the cream floor slab (AREA_COLOR_EXPR = "#f2eee6", layer-definitions.ts:4) and the near-white walls (WALL_COLOR = "#ebeae7"). The new fill #EFD3C8 is pale and close to both — check a shape is still visible on the map and in 3D. If it disappears, raise it rather than silently keeping the old brown; the outline colour #FA9E3D is the obvious alternative for the 3D/map body.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Doors render as a #EEC7E7-filled band outlined in #EE118A, thicker than today; swing arc/leaf in the outline colour.
  • Windows render in #2C9599, thicker than today, still as the glass double-line.
  • Rectangles, circles and polygons render #EFD3C8 filled, #FA9E3D outlined — committed shapes, drafts, group bounding box and handles alike.
  • Walls are visibly thicker and are still strokes, not bands — curved walls included.
  • Hover and selected states remain clearly distinct from the resting colours for every object type.
  • Clickable/hit areas are unchanged.
  • Shapes with an explicit color keep it, and the per-shape colour picker still changes a shape's colour — in the canvas, in 3D and on the map.
  • A shape with no explicit colour renders in the new default in 3D and on the map, and stays visible against the cream floor and near-white walls.
  • Readable in both light and dark mode.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Palette — src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/palette.ts, with the new doorFill field added to Palette in context.ts:

Token Value
C.door #EE118A
C.doorFill #EEC7E7 (new)
C.win #2C9599
C.shapeStroke #FA9E3D
C.shapeFill #EFD3C8

Door — was a dashed line, so there was nothing to fill. It is now a filled band across the opening: the span offset perpendicular by DOOR_PX / 2 either side, filled #EEC7E7 and stroked #EE118A. The swing leaf + arc keep the outline colour, thickened 1.2 → 1.6.

Wall — heavier stroke, still a stroke. No fill, no band; straight and bezier walls both go through the same lineWidth.

Window — unchanged two-line glass render, recoloured to #2C9599, line width 2 → 3 and the gap between the two lines 1.6 → 2.4.

Weights moved to constants (constants.ts) instead of inline literals scattered through draw.ts, so they can be tuned against the design in one place:

export const WALL_PX = 5, DOOR_PX = 7, WINDOW_PX = 3, WINDOW_GAP_PX = 2.4;

Hover/selected add +1/+2 at the draw site and still resolve through C.hot / C.sel, so selection stays legible against the new colours. Endpoint handles, the add-tool preview, shape handles and the group bounding box all read the palette tokens, so they picked the new colours up with no extra edits. Hit-test tolerances are independent of stroke width — nothing about what is clickable changed.

3D + map follow-through — SHAPE_COLOR repointed #8a7a5c → #EFD3C8. That is the single default behind all three non-canvas surfaces: the 3D mesh (scene3d.ts:243), the map fill + extrusion (geojson-utils.ts:497 → ["get","color"]), and the shape panel's default swatch (selection.ts:42). All three read shape.color ?? SHAPE_COLOR, so the per-shape colour picker is untouched — a shape the user recoloured keeps its colour, only the unset default moved. Doors and windows have no colour in 3D or on the map (they are cut-outs in the wall geometry), so there was nothing to recolour.

Two things worth eyeballing before this goes out — both are visual calls, not defects:

  1. #EFD3C8 is pale and close to the map's cream floor slab (#f2eee6) and near-white walls (#ebeae7); the old #8a7a5c was dark specifically to separate from them. Shapes may read faint on the map / in 3D. If so, #FA9E3D is the obvious body colour there.
  2. The shape fill is now fully opaque (it was alpha 0.10), so a shape hides the backdrop floorplan underneath it. That is the literal spec — say the word and it becomes an alpha.

Files

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/palette.ts — the four colours + doorFill

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/context.ts — doorFill on Palette

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/constants.ts — weights, SHAPE_COLOR

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts — door band, wall/window weights

  • Branch: feature/407-editor-palette-restyle · Commit: 4375667

  • pnpm lint · tsc --noEmit green. (Canvas draw layer — no unit-test harness; the change is colour tokens plus the door's band geometry, which mirrors the window's existing perpendicular-offset maths.) The 2 suite failures (renameSweep.test.ts, api/upload/route.test.ts EACCES on /tmp) pre-date this branch and are unrelated.

issues.display_title: Issue #409: Editor: cut the wall line at door/window openings, and make the door swing area clickable
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor 2D canvas — follow-up to #407.

Description

Two problems with how doors and windows sit in a wall on the 2D canvas.

1. The wall line runs straight through its own openings. A door or window is an opening cut into the wall, but the wall stroke is drawn over the full span, so the wall line shows through the door band and between the window's two glass lines. The wall should be interrupted where an opening sits.

2. A door's swing area isn't clickable. Only the thin door band responds to a click. The swing sector — the quarter-circle the leaf sweeps — is visibly part of the door but ignores clicks. It should select the door, and the selected door should show a fill on that sector.

Root cause

1. Walls are drawn as a single unbroken stroke, straight or bezier, with no knowledge of openings (draw.ts:146-163):

c2.beginPath(); c2.moveTo(ax, ay);
if (wl.h1x !== undefined) { ...bezierCurveTo... } else { c2.lineTo(bx, by); }
c2.stroke();

They are also painted after doors and windows, so the wall covers them. Since #407 the door band is an opaque fill, which makes the overlap obvious; the window's two glass lines have always had the wall showing through the gap between them.

The cut itself is a solved problem elsewhere: the 3D scene computes exactly these holes with wallOpenings() + keptSegments() and extrudes only the kept spans (scene3d.ts:184-187), and the map does the same (geojson-utils.ts:388-389). Only the 2D canvas skips it — which is also why the canvas can show a solid wall where the 3D preview shows an opening.

2. hitDoor is just hitSeg against the door's own chord (hittest.ts:56) — a BODY_R band around the segment, nothing more. The swing geometry only exists inline inside the renderer's local leaf() closure (draw.ts:94-115), in screen space, so nothing else can hit-test or fill it.

Scope

Wall cut

  • Cut the 2D wall stroke at its openings using the same wallOpenings() / keptSegments() the 3D scene uses, and the same tolerance (max(model.w, model.h) * 0.03), so the canvas and the 3D preview agree on where the openings are.
  • Gate on ctx.showDoors / ctx.showWindows exactly as scene3d does — hiding doors must restore a solid wall.
  • Curved walls carry no openings (the opening-drop never targets them), so they keep drawing as one unbroken bezier.
  • lineCap = "round" is already set for walls, so each kept span gets rounded ends — the doorjambs read soft, matching the 3D scene's joint caps.

Door swing sector

  • Extract the swing geometry into a pure world-space helper that returns the sector ring(s) — one for a single door, two half-length leaves for a double, none for swingType: "none". One source for the render, the selected fill and the hit-test, so the three can't drift (same pattern as shapeBoundary() / shapeHandles()).
  • The ring runs hinge → open-leaf endpoint → arc back to the closed position, so stroking it as an open path reproduces today's leaf line + arc exactly.
  • hitDoor falls back to a point-in-polygon test against those sectors when the band misses, returning the same door index.
  • Fill the sector when the door is selected; the sector's stroke follows the selected/hover colour like the band already does, so hovering the swing area gives feedback before the click.

Notes

  • hitDoor already runs before hitWall and before room-interior selection in onPointerDown, so a click in the swing area resolves to the door without reordering anything. It is also already gated on ctx.showDoors at the call site.
  • hitWall keeps testing the full chord: the gaps are covered by hitDoor/hitWindow, which run first, and when an opening is hidden the wall is drawn solid again and its hit-test is skipped — so the two stay consistent.
  • Wall length labels and endpoint handles keep using the whole wall; only the painted stroke is cut.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A wall is visibly interrupted where a door or window sits — no wall line through the door band, none between the window's two glass lines.
  • Hiding doors (or windows) restores the solid wall across those openings.
  • Curved walls are unaffected.
  • The 2D canvas and the 3D preview show openings in the same places.
  • Clicking anywhere in a door's swing sector selects that door.
  • A selected door shows a fill on its swing sector; hovering the sector highlights the door.
  • Doors with swingType: "none" are unaffected (band-only hit area, no sector).
  • Double doors are clickable on both leaves.
  • Wall selection, wall length labels and all endpoint handles behave as before.
  • Unit tests for the sector geometry (single / double / none, hinge end, swing side) and for the kept-span cut.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

1. Wall cut at openings — src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts

The wall stroke is now built from the kept spans rather than one moveTo/lineTo across the whole wall:

const holes = mergeIntervals([
  ...wallOpenings(wl, ctx.showDoors ? model.doors : [], openTol).holes,
  ...wallOpenings(wl, ctx.showWindows ? (model.windows ?? []) : [], openTol).holes,
]);
for (const [t0, t1] of keptSegments(holes)) { c2.moveTo(...); c2.lineTo(...); }

Same wallOpenings() + keptSegments() the 3D scene (scene3d.ts:184) and the map (geojson-utils.ts:388) already use, at the same tolerance (max(model.w, model.h) * 0.03) — so the canvas can no longer show a solid wall where the 3D preview shows an opening. Gated on showDoors / showWindows exactly as scene3d does, so hiding an opening restores the solid wall. keptSegments([]) already returns [[0, 1]], so a wall with no openings needs no special case. Curved walls keep drawing as one unbroken bezier. The wall's existing lineCap = "round" now rounds each doorjamb.

2. Door swing sector — src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts

doorSwingSectors(d, steps) is a new pure world-space helper returning the sector ring(s): one for a single door, two half-length leaves for a double, none for "none" / undefined / zero-length. Each ring runs hinge → open-leaf endpoint → arc back to the closed position, chosen so that tracing it as an open path reproduces the previous leaf line + arc exactly, while closing it gives the fillable sector. That is what makes it a single source for the render, the selected fill and the hit-test — the geometry previously lived only inside the renderer's local leaf() closure, in screen space, where nothing else could reach it.

hitDoor (hittest.ts) is no longer a bare hitSeg: it tries the band first (the door itself wins when both match), then falls back to point-in-polygon against the sectors, topmost door first. It already ran before hitWall and before room-interior selection in onPointerDown, and is already gated on ctx.showDoors at the call site, so nothing needed reordering.

A selected door fills its sector (alpha(C.doorSel, 0.18)), and the sector stroke now follows the selected/hover colour like the band already did — so the swing area highlights on hover, making the new hit region visible before the click.

hitWall deliberately still tests the full chord: the gaps are covered by hitDoor/hitWindow, which run first, and when an opening is hidden the wall is drawn solid and its hit-test is skipped — so render and hit-test stay consistent either way.

issues.display_title: Issue #412: Editor: Add Door / Add Window must only place an opening on a straight wall
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor tools — reported by Galuh (2026-07-27).

Description

tambahan fitur add windows jeung add door cuman bisa di wall

tambahan info windows jeung door cuman bisa ditambahkan di straight wall. ieu kondisi ketika user nambahkan di curved wall jeung object selain wall

Add Door and Add Window must only place an opening on a straight wall. Clicking a curved wall, a shape, an area or empty canvas must refuse the placement and say why, instead of silently creating something.

Root cause

onPointerDown auto-drops an opening only when the click lands on a straight wall (interactions.ts:136-139):

if ((ctx.addKind === "door" || ctx.addKind === "window") && !ctx.pendingP1) {
  const wi = hitWall(ctx, e.offsetX, e.offsetY);
  if (wi >= 0 && model.walls[wi].h1x === undefined) { addOpeningOnWall(ctx, wi, wx, wy, ctx.addKind); return; }
}

Every other click — curved wall, shape, area, empty canvas — falls through to a generic two-click free-draw block (interactions.ts:140-152) that pushes a door/window straight into the model at whatever two points the user clicked, attached to nothing. No warning, no feedback.

A floating opening is not just cosmetic — it does not exist anywhere except the 2D canvas. Doors and windows are never rendered as objects: the 3D scene and the map derive them as holes cut out of a wall via wallOpenings() (scene3d.ts:184-185, geojson-utils.ts:388-389), and wallOpenings only produces a hole for an opening that is collinear with and close to that wall. So an opening not on a wall:

  • is invisible in the 3D preview and on the published map — no wall to cut, so nothing is drawn;
  • never follows a wall when it moves — wallForOpening() returns null for it (#405);
  • ignores Align Left/Center/Right, which also resolve through wallForOpening() (commands.ts:103).

Curved walls are excluded for the same structural reason: the curved-wall extrusion path carries no opening bookkeeping at all (scene3d.ts:172-180 — "Curved walls carry no doors/windows in v1"), so an opening dropped on one would likewise never appear in 3D.

Scope

  • Add Door / Add Window accept a click only on a straight wall; the opening auto-drops there as it does today.
  • A click on a curved wall is refused with a message saying openings need a straight wall.
  • A click on anything else (shape, area, marker, empty canvas) is refused with a message saying the opening must go on a wall.
  • Refusals use the editor's existing status(ctx, msg, true) channel, already surfaced as the red action toast in the editor UI (FloorplanEditor.tsx:512) — no new UI.
  • The tool stays armed after a refusal, so the user can immediately click the right place.
  • Delete the two-click free-draw fallback for openings, and the state that only it used (pendingP1: its context field, initialiser, resets, the rubber-band preview in draw.ts, and its term in isInteracting). Nothing else sets or reads it. The addKind === "wall" branch inside that block is already unreachable — the wall tool returns earlier via wallClick().

Notes

  • Existing floating openings in saved projects are left alone — this only stops new ones. They were already invisible in 3D and on the map; nothing changes for them.
  • hitWall tolerance (BODY_R) is what decides "on a wall", the same test used for selecting a wall — so if a wall is clickable it is a valid drop target.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Clicking a straight wall in Add Door / Add Window drops the opening on it, exactly as today.
  • Clicking a curved wall creates nothing and shows a message naming the straight-wall requirement.
  • Clicking a shape, an area, a marker or empty canvas creates nothing and shows a message saying it must be on a wall.
  • No two-click free-draw path can create a door or window off a wall any more.
  • The tool remains active after a refused click.
  • Escape / switching tools still cancels cleanly.
  • pendingP1 is gone with no leftover references.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

A straight wall is now the only target Add Door / Add Window accepts — src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interactions.ts:

if (ctx.addKind === "door" || ctx.addKind === "window") {
  const wi = hitWall(ctx, e.offsetX, e.offsetY);
  if (wi < 0) status(ctx, `a ${ctx.addKind} can only be added on a wall — click a wall`, true);
  else if (model.walls[wi].h1x !== undefined) status(ctx, `a ${ctx.addKind} can only be added on a straight wall, not a curved one`, true);
  else addOpeningOnWall(ctx, wi, wx, wy, ctx.addKind);
  return;
}

Refusals go through the editor's existing status(ctx, msg, true) channel, already rendered as the red action toast — no new UI. The tool stays armed, so the next click can land on a wall without re-picking it.

Deleted, not disabled. The generic two-click free-draw block is gone, and with it pendingP1 — the state only it used: the EditorContext field, its initialiser, its resets in model-sync.ts / commands.ts / interaction-tools.ts, the rubber-band preview in draw.ts, and its term in isInteracting. The addKind === "wall" branch inside that block was already unreachable (the wall tool returns earlier via wallClick()). Net -28 lines.

issues.display_title: Issue #416: Editor: dragging a door/window must slide it along its wall, never off it
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor 2D canvas.

Description

Dragging a door or window lets it leave its wall: it can be pushed off the wall centerline, stretched far longer than the wall opening, and it drags the wall's own corner along with it. The result is a wall gaping open across a span no opening should cover.

Dragging an opening should slide it along the wall it is cut into — staying on the wall's line, keeping its size, and stopping at the wall's ends.

Root cause

An opening is dragged as a free 2D object. On pointer-down the drag set is built with joinGroup on both of its endpoints (interactions.ts:193 for doors, :201 for windows):

ctx.pending = [...joinGroup(ctx, { o: d, kx: "x1", ky: "y1" }), ...joinGroup(ctx, { o: d, kx: "x2", ky: "y2" })];

and every frame translates each ref by the raw pointer delta (interactions.ts:288). Nothing ties the motion to the wall, so any drag with a perpendicular component walks the opening off it.

The stretching has a specific cause. joinGroup is pointsAt(model, x, y, JOIN_EPS) with JOIN_EPS = 3 (constants.ts:5) — it collects every endpoint within 3 units, walls included. And alignOpeningOnWall parks an opening margin = 2 from the wall end (editing.ts:75). Since 2 < 3, any opening that has been through Align Left or Align Right has an endpoint inside the join radius of the wall's corner — so dragging that opening drags the wall corner with it, stretching the wall. The same applies to an opening drawn or nudged near a wall end.

Dragging an opening's endpoint handle has the same problem from the other direction (interactions.ts:187): free 2D motion plus a join group, so it resizes the opening off the wall and can drag the wall corner too.

Once the opening is off the wall line, wallForOpening() stops matching it, and it silently becomes the invisible floating opening described in #412 — gone from the 3D preview and the published map.

The pieces to fix this already exist: projectOnWall() (geometry.ts) gives the parameter of a point along a wall, and openingParamOnWall() / placeOpeningOnWall() (#405) already capture and restore an opening's position along its wall.

Scope

  • Dragging an opening's body slides it along its wall: project the pointer onto the wall for the parameter t, keep the opening's length and stored direction, and clamp so it never hangs off either end (placeOpeningOnWall already clamps).
  • Preserve the grab offset — record where along the opening the user grabbed it, so it doesn't jump its centre to the cursor on the first frame.
  • Dragging an opening's endpoint handle moves that end along the wall only, keeping the other end fixed, clamped to the wall and to a minimum length so it can't collapse or invert.
  • Neither drag uses joinGroup any more, so an opening can never move a wall.
  • The opening stays selected while its handle is dragged (today the handle branch clears selOps).
  • A legacy opening that is not on any wall (wallForOpening returns null) keeps the current free translate — there is no wall to slide along. New ones can't be created since #412.
  • Undo covers the whole gesture, as the other drags do (one pushUndo when the drag passes DRAG_MIN).

Notes

  • Resize also has a precise control already — the opening-width slider (setSelectedOpeningWidth) — so the handle drag only needs to stay sane, not to be the primary sizing tool.
  • No grid snapping along the wall: an opening's position on a wall is continuous, and snapping t to the world grid would fight the wall's angle. Its ends already clamp to the wall.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Dragging a door or window slides it along its wall and it never leaves the wall line.
  • Its length is unchanged by a body drag.
  • It stops at each end of the wall instead of hanging off.
  • Grabbing it anywhere along its length does not make it jump on the first frame.
  • Dragging an opening — body or handle — never moves, stretches or rotates a wall, including an opening sitting within JOIN_EPS of a wall corner after Align Left/Right.
  • Dragging an endpoint handle resizes the opening along the wall, keeps the other end fixed, and cannot collapse or invert it.
  • The opening stays selected throughout.
  • One undo restores the pre-drag position.
  • An opening not on any wall still drags freely.
  • Unit tests for the slide (grab offset, clamping at both ends) and the endpoint move (clamp, minimum length).
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Dragging an opening is now one parameter along its wall, not a (dx, dy).

New pure helper — src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/editing.ts:

placeOpeningEndOnWall(op, wall, end, t, minLen = 1) moves one end of an opening to parameter t along its wall, leaving the other end fixed. The dragged end is clamped onto the wall and kept minLen from the fixed end. Its side comes from where that end already sits, not from the pointer — so dragging past the fixed end stops at minLen instead of mirroring the opening through it. (The first pass derived the side from the pointer; the test caught the inversion.)

Wiring — src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interactions.ts:

  • beginOpeningSlide(ctx, op, wx, wy, end) arms ctx.openingSlide at pointer-down: it resolves the wall via wallForOpening(), captures the opening's position with openingParamOnWall() (#405), and records grabDt — where along the opening the user grabbed it — so the centre doesn't jump to the cursor on the first frame. Returns false for an opening on no wall, and the caller falls back to a free translate.
  • Each drag frame projects the pointer onto the wall (projectOnWall) and re-places the opening from the captured anchor: placeOpeningOnWall for a body drag (length and direction preserved, clamped at both wall ends), placeOpeningEndOnWall for a handle.
  • Neither path goes through joinGroup any more, which is what let an opening drag a wall corner.
  • The opening stays selected while its handle is dragged; that branch used to clear selOps.
  • ctx.openingSlide joins the other drag state in endPointer, setCursor and isInteracting.

No grid snap along the wall: a position on a wall is continuous, and snapping t to the world grid would fight the wall's angle.

issues.display_title: Issue #418: Editor: repeated clicks in one spot should step down through overlapping objects
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor 2D canvas — selection.

Description

Objects overlap on the canvas, and only the topmost one is ever reachable by clicking. A shape sits inside a room; a door or window sits in a wall; the wall sits against a room. Today the click always resolves to whichever is highest in the hit-test order, and there is no way to reach what is underneath without moving the shapes out of the way.

Clicking repeatedly in the same spot should step down through what is under the cursor.

  • Shape: 1st click selects the shape → 2nd click selects the room it sits in.
  • Door / window: 1st click selects the opening → 2nd click selects the wall it is cut into → 3rd click selects the room.
  • The last step is always a room — the one under the cursor, or the nearest room if the cursor is not inside one (e.g. clicking a wall on the building's outer edge).

Current behaviour

onPointerDown walks a fixed priority chain and returns at the first match (interactions.ts:166-270):

annotation → group handle → shape handle → endpoint handle → door → window → wall → shape → manual area → room

Every click re-runs the same chain from the top, so the same object wins every time. Nothing records that the previous click was at the same point, so there is no notion of "the one below".

Design

Candidate stack. A pure hitStack(ctx, sx, sy) returning every selectable target under the cursor, ordered exactly as the existing chain already prefers them, so a first click behaves identically to today:

  1. annotation (point / safety)
  2. door
  3. window
  4. wall
  5. shape
  6. manual area
  7. the room containing the point
  8. the nearest room — appended only when no room contains the point, so the cycle always has a room to end on

Cycle state. ctx.clickCycle: { sx, sy, depth } | null. On a plain pointer-down: if the click is within a few px of the previous one and the stack is unchanged, depth = (depth + 1) % stack.length; otherwise depth = 0. Select stack[depth].

Resets — anything that means "this is a new click, not a repeat": the pointer moving beyond the tolerance, an actual drag (past DRAG_MIN), a tool change, Escape, or a selection made any other way.

Scope

  • Add hitStack() alongside the existing hit-tests, built from them — not a second implementation of the same geometry.
  • Add nearestRoom() — the room whose polygon is closest to the cursor, for the final rung. Needs a point-to-polygon distance helper (labelPoint already has this maths inline and un-exported; extract rather than duplicate).
  • Drive selection in onPointerDown from hitStack + clickCycle, keeping each kind's existing selection side effects (a door/window still arms its wall-slide from #416, a wall still arms its drag group, a shape still arms its shape-drag).
  • Wrap around: a click past the last candidate returns to the top.

Not in scope — deliberately

  • Handles are not depth layers. The endpoint / resize handles and the group bounding box are drag affordances of an already-selected object. A second click on a handle must keep dragging that handle, not step behind it — so they stay ahead of the cycle and never enter the stack.
  • Additive clicks are not cycles. Shift / Ctrl / Cmd click and the marquee build a multi-selection; repeating one there must keep toggling, not descend.
  • Hover highlighting keeps following the topmost object — the cycle is a click behaviour, not a hover one.

Notes / gotchas found while scoping

  • selectRoom(ctx, i) toggles off when that room is already the sole selection (selection.ts): ctx.selRooms = ctx.selRooms.length === 1 && ctx.selRooms[0] === i ? [] : [i]. Used as-is for a cycle step, the click that should select the room would clear the selection instead. The cycle needs a non-toggling select.
  • Detected-room selection is deferred to endPointer via roomPending + panPending, so dragging from inside a room pans instead of selecting. Manual areas select immediately. Both behaviours must survive — a room reached by cycling still has to allow drag-to-pan.
  • Walls are hit-tested before shapes today, so a shape lying over a wall resolves to the wall first. Keeping the stack in the existing order preserves that; the shape is simply the next step down.
  • hitDoor now also covers the swing sector (#409), so a click in the swing area cycles from the same stack as the door band.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Clicking a shape selects the shape; clicking again without moving selects the room it sits in.
  • Clicking a door or window selects it; again → its wall; again → the room.
  • When the cursor is not inside any room, the final step selects the nearest room.
  • The first click at any point selects exactly what it selects today.
  • Moving the cursor away and clicking starts a fresh cycle from the top.
  • Dragging (not clicking) never advances the cycle.
  • Clicking past the last candidate wraps back to the first.
  • Shift / Ctrl / Cmd click still toggles multi-selection instead of cycling.
  • Clicking a handle still drags that handle, at any point in a cycle.
  • Dragging from inside a room still pans.
  • Each selected kind keeps its drag behaviour: openings slide on their wall, walls drag with their openings, shapes move/resize.
  • Unit tests for the stack order, the depth advance/reset rule, wrap-around, and nearest-room.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

hitStack(ctx, sx, sy, wx, wy) (editor/hittest.ts) returns everything selectable under the cursor, in the order the click chain already preferred them — so stack[0], a first click, selects exactly what it selected before, and each further entry is one step down. A room is always appended last (the one containing the cursor, else nearestRoom), so the cycle bottoms out somewhere useful; the nearest-room fallback only applies when something else is already in the stack, so bare canvas still clears and pans.

cycleDepth(prev, sx, sy, len, eps) is pure and unit-tested. It anchors on the run's first click, not the previous one — anchoring on the previous click would let a 2px drift per click walk a cycle across the canvas. (prev.depth + 1) % len also re-clamps for free when the stack under the cursor gets shorter.

The run is taken and cleared at the top of onPointerDown, so every early return — a tool, a handle, a marker — ends it without needing its own reset line; only the stack dispatch starts a new one. Drags and pans end it in endPointer.

Dispatch moved into selectTarget(), one branch per kind, each keeping the drag it already armed: openings slide on their wall (#416), walls drag with their joints and openings (#405), shapes move/resize. Rooms stay deferred to endPointer, so dragging from inside one still pans.

Outside the cycle, as designed: handles (drag affordances of an already-selected object, not depth layers), additive clicks (Shift/Ctrl keep toggling a multi-selection), and annotations (resolved first, they own their own multi-select and drag).

distanceToRing() / distanceToPolygon() added to geometry.ts for the nearest-room step; labelPoint()'s inline clearance loop was repeating the same point-to-segment maths and now calls distanceToRing.

The selectRoom toggle-off hazard flagged while scoping turned out to be a non-issue. The preceding cycle step (wall/shape) already clears selRooms, so the toggle condition selRooms.length === 1 && selRooms[0] === i can never be met when the cycle reaches the room. No change was needed there.

Follow-up — the cycle now covers every selectable object

Point and safety markers were the one selectable kind still outside the cycle (the original scope resolved them before it). They now lead the hit stack — they paint on top — so a second click reaches whatever is behind them.

Full stack: anno → door → window → wall → shape → manual area → room (under the cursor, else nearest).

Coverage check against everything with selection state (selWalls, selOps, selManual, selRooms, selShapes, selAnnos): markers were the only gap. model.icons stays out — it is the one drawable with no selection state at all, only a double-click rename, so there is nothing to cycle to.

Two subtleties this needed:

  1. The stack is resolved before anything is cleared, so the marker branch still sees the existing multi-selection — a plain click on an already-selected marker must keep the group so a drag moves all of it. Clearing selAnnos first would have broken multi-drag.
  2. A marker at the top of the stack is settled before the handle branches. A marker has always out-ranked a selected shape's resize handles; resolving the stack up front would silently have flipped that. Depth 0 on a marker returns early, preserving the old precedence — deeper steps fall through to the normal path where handles keep priority.

issues.display_title: Issue #421: Editor: a wall must not be shortened past the openings it carries
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Editor 2D canvas — follow-up to #405 / #416.

Description

Dragging a wall's endpoint can shorten it past the openings cut into it. The doors and windows pile up at the short end, overlapping each other and their swing arcs, and the wall ends up carrying more opening than it has length.

A wall should not be shortenable below the openings it holds: its minimum length is the combined width of its doors and windows.

Root cause

A wall endpoint drag translates the endpoint refs freely (interactions.ts, the ctx.drag branch of onPointerMove) — nothing consults what the wall carries.

The openings then follow correctly but independently: placeOpeningOnWall (#405) keeps each opening's length, caps it at the wall length, and clamps its centre so it can't hang off either end. Each opening obeys that on its own, with no knowledge of the others — so once the wall is shorter than their combined width, every one of them clamps into the same shrinking span and they stack on top of each other. The clamp is doing exactly what it was written to do; nothing owns the constraint between openings.

The information needed is already captured: ctx.openingDrag records { op, wall, at } for every opening on every dragged wall, and at.len is that opening's own length, taken before the drag. Summing at.len per wall gives the shortest that wall may become — no new state required.

Scope

  • While a wall drag is live, reject any frame that would take a dragged wall below the combined width of the openings it carries.
  • Revert that frame's delta and do not advance the drag origin, so the wall sticks at the limit and resumes cleanly when the pointer comes back — rather than the wall lagging behind the cursor by the rejected amount.
  • Derive the limit from ctx.openingDrag (at.len summed per wall). No new context state.
  • Applies to every wall in the drag group, so a shared corner that shortens two walls is limited by whichever hits its limit first.

Notes

  • At exactly the limit the openings sit flush end to end, which is fine — two windows side by side is a real thing. The limit is about not overlapping, not about spacing.
  • Curved walls carry no openings, so they are unaffected.
  • The wall body drag is a pure translation and never changes length; only endpoint / shared-corner drags can trip this.
  • Out of scope: the opening-width slider (setSelectedOpeningWidth) does not clamp against the wall either. Different entry point, worth its own look — flagging it here rather than widening this fix.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Dragging a wall endpoint stops when the wall reaches the combined width of its openings; it cannot be shortened further.
  • Openings on that wall never overlap each other as a result of a wall drag.
  • The wall keeps following the cursor normally in every other direction and once the pointer moves back.
  • A wall with no openings drags exactly as before.
  • A shared corner shortening two walls respects both walls' limits.
  • Lengthening a wall is never restricted.
  • One undo still restores the whole gesture.
  • Unit test for the per-wall minimum length.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

A wall drag frame is now rejected when the result is broken: a wall too short to hold one of its openings at full width, or two openings on the same wall that overlap. The delta is undone and the openings re-placed from their captured anchors, so the restore is exact. lastW deliberately stays put, so the wall sticks at the limit and picks the drag back up when the pointer returns, instead of trailing the cursor by everything that was rejected.

Correction to this issue's own plan

The scope above specified the limit as the openings' combined width. That is wrong, and a test caught it before merge.

An opening keeps its fraction along the wall (t), not an absolute offset. Two 10-wide openings sitting in the first fifth of a 100-long wall have a combined width of 20 — but shrinking that wall to 20 already stacks them, because both clamp to the same end. Sum-of-widths is only correct when the openings happen to be evenly spread.

So the check measures the placed result instead of predicting a minimum length. openingsOverlapOnWall(wall, ops) (new, in floorplan/editing.ts) projects each opening onto the wall, sorts the spans and looks for a real overlap. That also handles the mix of proportional placement and end clamping for free — which is exactly what makes any closed-form minimum position-dependent.

Flush end to end is allowed (a small epsilon) — two windows side by side is real. Walls with no openings and curved walls are unaffected. No new context state: the widths and anchors were already captured in ctx.openingDrag by #405.
